title: Elon survey finds Americans fear AI will hollow out the meaning of work
source_used: Elon University news release on its own survey (full text read)
key_facts: Elon University's Imagining the Digital Future Center ran the national survey; the polling firm SSRS fielded it on 20-24 Aug 2026 among 1,158 US adults (775 employed), online and by phone in English; margin of error +/-3.4 points.
83% of US adults expect AI to eliminate more jobs than it creates; 68% expect most jobs to pay too little for a decent lifestyle; 62% expect most available jobs to be dull and unfulfilling.
65% agree that if AI makes work less meaningful, people will lose their sense of purpose and dignity; 52% agree most workers will have little control over their futures.
Among workers, 66% say they are already comfortable using AI at work (25%) or would welcome it with more training (41%); half are highly confident they can adapt their skills.
Workers in households earning at least $100,000 are twice as likely as those under $50,000 to be comfortable with AI at work (34% vs 17%).
Only 22% of workers are extremely or very confident that employers would help them if AI affects their jobs, 11% for government agencies; 33% for family, friends and former colleagues.
Only 24% say local K-12 schools do a good job preparing students for a world using AI.
65% of adults used a large language model in the previous week; Lee Rainie, director of the center, calls the findings 'an enormous policy challenge'.
quote_evidence: In a new national survey by Elon University's Imagining the Digital Future Center, 83% of U.S. adults expect AI to eliminate more jobs than it creates, 68% expect most jobs to pay too little for a decent lifestyle and 62% expect most available jobs to be dull and unfulfilling.
Two-thirds of those who work (66%) say they are already comfortable using AI at work or would welcome it with more training
The survey included 1,158 U.S. adults and included an oversample that brings the number of workers participating in the survey to 775 adults employed full or part time.
why_it_matters_hint: A large national survey finds most Americans expect AI to bring fewer, lower-paid, less meaningful jobs, yet most workers are open to using it.
notes: Primary source: the university's own release on its own survey; the figures are the survey's, with a stated margin of error, and have no outside review. Not a follow-up of an earlier edition item.
